s.q: Sign scheme of a rational function
s.f: f(x)=\frac{(x-a_1)^{k_1}\cdots}{(x-b_1)^{m_1}\cdots}:\ \text{sign changes at a root of odd multiplicity only}
s.n: Mark critical points, start with $+$ on the far right (leading coefficient positive), flip sign only across odd-multiplicity points; exclude zeros of the denominator.
Never cross-multiply by an expression whose sign is unknown.

s.q: If an equation mixes $|x-a|$ terms or $x|x+a|$
s.f: \text{split at the zeros of each modulus; solve a quadratic in each interval}
s.n: 1) Mark critical points. 2) In each interval drop the bars with the right sign. 3) Solve and keep roots that lie inside that interval. For $|x-2|^2+|x-2|-2=0$ put $t=|x-2|\ge0$ directly.
s.h: Trap: a root found in an interval must be checked against that interval.

s.n: Rewrite as $|u|+|v|=|u+v|$ with $u,v$ chosen so the identity applies; then solve $uv\ge0$ by the wavy curve.

s.q: If it is a log equation/inequality with variable base or argument
s.n: 1) Write the domain: argument $>0$, base $>0$, base $\ne1$. 2) Factor the arguments to make $\log_a b\cdot\log_b a=1$ appear; put $t=\log$. 3) Solve, then intersect with the domain.
